chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Ayyub al-Madani, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Husayn al-Ahmasi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The heart relies upon the written (words).

key_terms.الْقَلْبُ: Heart — the seat of understanding and intellect in Islamic thought
key_terms.الْكِتَابَةِ: Writing, the written word — preserving knowledge in textual form
key_terms.يَتَّكِلُ: Relies upon, trusts, leans on — expressing dependence and confidence

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the heart's reliance on writing?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that the human heart trusts and depends upon that which is written down. This hadith, recorded in the chapter on the merits of writing and attachment to books, emphasizes the importance of preserving religious knowledge in written form, as the heart finds stability and certainty in the written word. In the early Islamic scholarly tradition, this was understood as an exhortation to compile and preserve hadith in written records rather than relying solely on memory.
